steps.text: Heat oil in large pot over medium-low heat. Place onion, zucchini, yellow squash, and carrot in pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until onions begin to soften and turn translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the red and yellow peppers and mushrooms; cook another 3 minutes. Vegetables should still be firm.

Pour in the vegetable stock and season with paprika, cardamom, salt, and cilantro. Bring mixture to a boil; reduce heat to low. Stir in chickpeas and tomatoes. Slowly pour in the couscous; stir. Cover pot immediately and remove from the heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff couscous with a fork. The couscous should have absorbed about half the cooking liquid.
Serve at slightly warmer than room temperature. Garnish with orange zest and the grated cheese, paprika, and almonds.

raw_recipe.headline: 25-Minute Tunisian Vegetable Couscous
raw_recipe.description: A quick, versatile way to prepare couscous with summer vegetables -- zucchini, yellow squash, and bell peppers, with mushrooms and chickpeas. This fragrant dish is seasoned with smoky paprika, cardamom, and orange zest.
raw_recipe.name: 25-Minute Tunisian Vegetable Couscous

review.reviewBody: Tons of veggies. NOT enough spice. Double everything, add garlic.

Start with a big soup pot (I started with a large frying pan, but it was soon overwhelmed). Added 2-3 cloves garlic to the onion stage, couple stalks of chopped celery along with the carrot, added Garam Marsala instead of Cardamom & tripled all of the spices, used diced canned tomatoes & tri-colored couscous, stirred in 1 cup raisins (chopped dates would also be good) at the end. Would have taken 25 minutes if I did not have to chop anything; probably closer to 2 hours with the chopping. Makes a lot, so it was perfect for the neighborhood party.

Super yummy. I did add twice the spice and some turmeric, which turned the whole dish a lovely golden color. I wanted to add if using Israeli (also called Pearl) couscous, you will need to cook for a few more minutes before taking off the heat, or else the couscous won't be cooked all the way through. Very forgiving recipe - I would imagine you could toss in any veg you have on hand and it would still be fantastic. I also toasted the dry couscous for 5 - 7 min before adding to the pot, and finished the whole dish with the juice of one squeezed lemon, because I like things lemony. Thank you!

Used 1/2 the vegetable quantities in recipe except for the courgette and mushrooms which I did not reduce .Used my own judgement on spices based on experience and used juice from a small orange instead of zest. I also cheated and used the 'instant' couscous and only 160ml of stock as it was for 2 persons only which meant the veg/couscous ratio was better. Hubby liked it a lot and I thought it really tasty.Excellent basic recipe to adapt to one's own taste.

A very easy and forgiving recipe. Can be easily modified to suit one's preferences. I didn't have the issue with prep time that some others mentioned; it took me about 15 minutes to get everything chopped and ready to go. I used whole grain Israeli coucous, so I cooked that with veg broth, but separate from the veggies. After both were done, I stirred them together and let them cook for a few more minutes to blend the flavors. I did make a cpl of modifications based on what I had - I was out of cilantro and cardamom, so left that out, and I added some minced garlic and curry powder. I also left out the orange zest because I am not a fan of orange. I am curious to try it again with the cilantro, as that is one of my favorite flavors. I also think some asparagus might be a nice addition. I will definitely be adding this into my regular rotation of favorites. Love the simplicity, and a great meal to whip up after work.

I have made this several times, and it is very good with a few changes.. I leave out the zucchini and squash because I don't like them, and use chicken broth instead of vegetable for more flavor. I also use more like 3 1/4 cups broth instead of four. I double the recommended spices and add onion powder, garlic powder, garlic, hot sauce, parsley and white pepper. Also, I mix grated parmesan cheese into the whole dish. I serve with the Indonesian Satay on this website..

Amazing! Couple of things- definitely double the spices as suggested- perfect that way. You definitely need to put it in a pot- it does make a ton...but that's because the serving size is listed for six.:) I didn't have cardamom so I substituted cinnamon- perfect. I added a clove of garlic as suggested- perfect. FYI- one box of couscous only has 1.5 cups of dry couscous unless you get the bigger one (oops!). Last, Im not sure why someeople said it takes two hours total with prep. I timed it from start to finish- took 39 min. Cut up the onion, zucchini, squash And carrot, put in pot. While that is going, cut up the rest of the stuff. Delicious.

I always add my own flare. I actually did add @ 4 cloves of finely chopped garlic & a couple pats of butter. I put green, yellow, orange & red bell peppers. I substituted allspice for cardamom and added big pinch of Montreal Steak seasoning plus a good dash of Adobo seasoning. I threw in a couple of fresh sage leaves for good measure. Turned out pretty good! Definitely HALVE this recipe unless you are cooking for a Large crowd!!

I loved this. Start to finish 20 minutes. Beware this makes ALOT of food (more like 10 servings the way I eat). But totally worth it. I agree with the other reviewers when it comes to the spices. Double it, and I also added 1 T. cumin and 2T. of tomato paste and a can of tomato sauce. I like tomatos.

Fast and easy to make but very tasty. I read reviews first and decided to double the spice the recipe called for. I also added garlic and some cajun spices. Definitely recommend adding the Parmesan too!

Great, yummy, easy, quick, and healthy dinner! I did not have any peppers so instead I added 3 celery stalks (at the same time as the onions). I also did not have the spices, so I used 1tsp. garam masala - which has most of the spices needed plus some others. I added about 1 tsp. of granulated garlic. Lastly I did not have chickpeas so I just left those out. I topped it with Lemon Zest. It was fabulous!!! My mom LOVED it, and so did the toddler, and husband! Thanks! I gave it 5 stars because it was so easy and obviously a flexible meal.

I love this and have made it many times. I substitute different vegetables based on what I have from my own garden and what is in the fridge already. This is great for a meatless meal added to your weekly menu.
Amazing. So easy to make

The couscous soaked up all of the broth, which was fine. I added garlic, and substituted curry, cumin, and red pepper for the spices. I liked the ease of cooking the couscous in the same broth with the vegetables.

Needs more spices!! The basic recipe was good but I like alittle more spice on the taste buds. It sure did make alot more than expected. I split this recipe in half (3 servings) and it was enough for 1 1/2 cups for 3 people.
Added Garlic!

We followed the recipe exactly with the exception of substituting cinnamon for cardamom as we didn't have any. The flavors of the spices were subtle, but that allowed for enjoying the flavors of the vegetables as well. We topped it with toasted almonds and orange zest and thought it was very nice. I recruited my husband to help chop veg, as I was worried that it would take a long time. If I were doing it on my own, I really don't think it would take that much longer, as we were finished chopping well before the vegetables were due to be added. From start to finish, it took 33 minutes to get it on the table. My kids both liked it too and everyone said it was "make again"! Thanks for a great, easy, healthy recipe!
Wonderful! My family loved the flavor in this. A good recipe to incorporate more veggies and have lots of flavor. Yummy!

Excellent dish! I do like a bit more spice; however the majority of my family likes to taste the flavor of the ingredients - not the spice, and they enjoyed it very much! (I did as well, it was quite tasty) Great recipe!

I doubled the spices like other reviewers had mentioned and it was quite good! I used whole wheat couscous and 5 minutes wasn't enough time to absorb the liquid so i left it covered for 10 minutes. Overall it was a good recipe and my family really enjoyed it!
